title: E-Math algebra: expansion, factorisation and changing the subject
subject: math

slots.label: Expand with the area model
entries: Expand with the area model: the tiles for (x + 2)(x + 3) land as x^2, 3x, 2x and 6 - collect the x tiles to get x^2 + 5x + 6.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Factorise by grouping
entries: Factorise by grouping: group 2x + 6 + xy + 3y into pairs, take 2 from the first pair and y from the second, then pull the common bracket (x + 3) out whole to get (x + 3)(2 + y).
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Change the subject to x
entries: Change the subject to x: undo y = 3x + 5 in reverse - subtract 5 first, then divide by 3 - to get x = (y - 5) / 3.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: The (a+b)^2 trap
entries: The (a+b)^2 trap: squaring a sum gives three terms, not two - with a = 2 and b = 3 the full value is 25, and the middle term 2ab is what makes the difference.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Expansion
entries: Multiplying out brackets so every term in one bracket multiplies every term in the other: (x + 2)(x + 3) expands to x^2 + 5x + 6.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Factorisation
entries: Writing an expression as a product of brackets, the reverse of expansion: 2x + 6 + xy + 3y factorises to (x + 3)(2 + y).
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Subject of formula
entries: The variable a formula is rearranged to give on its own: in x = (y - 5) / 3, taken from y = 3x + 5, the subject is x.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Identity
entries: A statement that is true for every value of the variables, like (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2, unlike an equation that holds only for some values.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Middle term
entries: The term between the two squared terms in the expansion of a squared bracket: 2ab in (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
